hero.title: A typeface built from Auckland's Arts Precinct
hero.intro: Toi o Tāmaki means "the art of Auckland" in te reo Māori. It is a display typeface drawn from the buildings around the city's Arts Precinct, where a Victorian art gallery, an Edwardian town hall and a modern timber canopy stand within a few streets of each other.

image.alt: The Toi o Tāmaki title above the first letters of the typeface, drawn as white line work on deep purple

sections.heading: A typeface for one part of the city

p: The brief imagined Auckland Council launching a promotional campaign, with a travel and tourism website, street displays and signage, and asked designers to submit a typeface that reflects one part of the city. Toi o Tāmaki is a concept design made in response to that brief.

I chose the Arts Precinct, in the heart of the city centre. It is home to the Auckland Art Gallery, the Central City Library, Aotea Square, the Town Hall, the Aotea Centre and the Civic Theatre, so [[old and new architecture stand on the same few streets]].

blocks.text: The precinct mixes old and new buildings on the same streets, so the typeface does the same.

bleed.alt: The kauri-lined canopy of the Auckland Art Gallery seen from below against a blue sky

p: I walked around the area with a camera and tried to capture what gives the precinct its feel. Two things kept coming up.

The first was the Auckland Art Gallery, which joins its original 1887 building, with its French Renaissance details, to the kauri-lined canopies added in 2011. The second was the [[Victorian and Edwardian architecture]] around the city centre, with its columns, arched windows, keystones and clock towers, from the gallery itself to the Town Hall.

blocks.text: The gallery holds the whole idea in one building: a Victorian facade with a modern timber canopy beside it.

sections.heading: Columns, arches, stairs and a canopy

p: Every letter is assembled from a small set of parts taken from those buildings, drawn as line work over a construction grid, like an architect's elevation. The same parts repeat from letter to letter, so [[even the most detailed ones belong to one set]].

blocks.title: Columns as stems
p: The upright strokes of letters such as b, d, h, i, l, p and q are classical columns, with fluted shafts and scrolled capitals like those on the older facades around the precinct. On its own, [[a single column already reads as architecture]], which makes it the simplest building block in the set.

image.alt: A Victorian facade with pilasters beside the letters i and l, drawn as fluted columns

blocks.title: Arches and keystones as bowls
p: The rounded parts of the a, m, n and o are arches, and most of them carry a keystone at the top, like the arched windows on the gallery and the Town Hall. The o is the simplest version: [[a ring of mouldings with one keystone]].

image.alt: The Auckland Art Gallery's clock tower and arched windows beside the letters n and o, each with a keystone at the top

blocks.title: Stairs inside the letters
p: Staircases fill the inside of the k, s and z, and a set of steps forms the base of the v. They bring in the steps and entrances that lead into these buildings, and they give the flatter letters [[a sense of depth]].

image.alt: The letters k, s and z, each with a staircase drawn inside it

blocks.title: The canopy as a crown
p: The flared, fanned shape on top of the t and z comes from the kauri canopy of the Art Gallery, the newest part of the precinct. It is [[the one modern element in the typeface]], and on the t it sits on top of a classical column, so the old and new parts of the precinct meet in a single letter.

image.alt: The Auckland Art Gallery's timber canopy beside the letters t and z, both topped with a fanned canopy shape

p: Seen together, the letters read like a row of facades. I drew every lowercase letter from a to z and kept the line weight and the grid the same throughout, so [[the decoration never breaks the set]].
The letters exist as Illustrator artwork. Turning them into a working font file is a step I have not taken yet, so for now every word is set by hand.

sections.heading: From photos to pencil to line work

p: The letters started in a sketchbook, mostly to test [[which building parts could carry a letter]]. Once a part worked, I redrew it in pencil and traced it in Illustrator.

blocks.alt: A desk with printed photos of the precinct's buildings laid out in rows in front of a keyboard

p: To show the typeface doing its job, I set a campaign line in it, Art is all around, for posters and street displays in the precinct. The line is short, so [[the letters do most of the talking]].
